questions.q: What does the table prefix usually tell you?
options: Which database server the table is on
Which module owns the table, e.g. AP_ for Payables, AR_ for Receivables
The table's creation date
Nothing — prefixes are random
questions.explain: Oracle Fusion table names are prefixed by module: AP_ Payables, AR_ Receivables, FA_ Fixed Assets, CE_ Cash Management, XLA_ Subledger Accounting, HZ_ Trading Community Architecture.

questions.q: What does the _ALL suffix on a table name mean?
options: The table includes rows for every business unit/operating context at once
The table has no primary key
The table is deprecated
The table only stores a single row
questions.explain: The _ALL suffix is a multi-org holdover meaning the table spans every business unit, so queries must scope it deliberately to avoid mixing unrelated data.

questions.q: What question does a business unit answer?
options: Which chart of accounts is used
Which operational entity a transaction was processed under
Which currency a journal is stored in
Which accounting period is open
questions.explain: A business unit is the operational boundary — which office, division, or operating company a transaction belongs to.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a base table and a view?
options: There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable
A view always has more columns than a base table
A base table is where data is physically stored, while a view is a saved query built on top of one or more base tables, often read-only
Views can never be documented by Oracle
questions.explain: Base tables hold the physically stored data; views, including the ones behind many OTBI subject areas, pre-join or pre-filter that data for reporting convenience.

questions.q: Which table stores supplier-level procurement attributes, and what is its primary key?
options: HZ_PARTIES, keyed by PARTY_ID
POZ_SUPPLIERS, keyed by VENDOR_ID
AP_INVOICES_ALL, keyed by INVOICE_ID
POZ_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL_M, keyed by VENDOR_SITE_ID
questions.explain: POZ_SUPPLIERS stores supplier-level attributes with primary key VENDOR_ID, a naming holdover from Oracle's older terminology.

questions.q: What does a row in HZ_PARTIES represent?
options: A general ledger journal entry
A supplier's bank account
A customer account with credit terms
A core identity (person, organization, or group) independent of any business relationship
questions.explain: HZ_PARTIES is the party-centric master identity table and carries no financial data or business-relationship detail on its own.

options: A general ledger account combination
A customer's bill-to usage of a site
A supplier's pay-site flag
A specific party's use of a specific location
questions.explain: HZ_PARTY_SITES is the generic link between a party and a location, representing that party's use of the address.

questions.q: Why is it risky to treat "scheduled," "applied," and "disbursed" as the same thing when answering "is this invoice paid"?
options: Scheduling always happens after disbursement
They are always identical in Oracle Fusion, so there's no risk
An invoice can be scheduled but not yet applied, or applied but not yet fully disbursed — collapsing the three into one answer can be wrong
Only "disbursed" exists; the other two states are fictional
questions.explain: Scheduled, applied, and disbursed are three distinct states tracked in different places, and an invoice can be in one state without yet being in another.

questions.q: Why are invoice lines and invoice distributions NOT the same thing?
options: They are the same thing, just named differently
A single invoice line can be split across multiple accounting distributions, so the distribution table captures a finer level of detail than the line
Distributions only exist for customer transactions, not supplier invoices
Lines always have exactly one distribution, with no exceptions
questions.explain: A single line's amount can be split across multiple distributions, each potentially posting to a different account — that split is what AP_INVOICE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL stores.

questions.q: What does the LINE_TYPE column on RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_LINES_ALL distinguish?
options: Which business unit owns the line
Whether a line represents the billed item (LINE), tax (TAX), or freight (FREIGHT), among others
Which supplier the line belongs to
The ledger currency
questions.explain: LINE_TYPE distinguishes different kinds of amounts within the same transaction, such as the billed goods/services, tax, and freight.

questions.q: What three ideas repeat across both the AP and AR chains?
options: Party, account, site
A header carrying the total, lines explaining what it's made of, and a separate money-matching table
Ledger, period, balance
Business unit, data access set, role
questions.explain: Both chains reduce to the same three structural ideas, just with different table names and vocabulary.

questions.q: What is stored in XLA_AE_HEADERS and XLA_AE_LINES?
options: The supplier's party identity
The raw invoice lines
The subledger's own journal entry (header and debit/credit lines), generated from an accounting event
The general ledger's posted balances
questions.explain: XLA_AE_HEADERS and XLA_AE_LINES represent the subledger-level journal entry produced for an accounting event, before it reaches GL.

questions.q: What is the difference between ENTERED_DR/ENTERED_CR and ACCOUNTED_DR/ACCOUNTED_CR?
options: Entered amounts are in the transaction's entered currency; accounted amounts are converted into the ledger's functional currency
Entered amounts are always in USD
Accounted amounts only apply to manual journals
There is no difference — they are always identical
questions.explain: For a foreign-currency transaction, the entered and accounted amount pairs can differ; for a transaction already in the ledger's currency, they match.

options: The business transaction (invoice, receipt, depreciation run, etc.) in a generic way SLA can work with regardless of its source subledger
A customer's bill-to site
The supplier's bank account
The ledger's chart of accounts
questions.explain: XLA_TRANSACTION_ENTITIES is the generic representation of the source transaction, independent of which subledger it came from.

questions.q: What happens if a period is Permanently Closed and a correction is needed?
options: The ledger itself must be deleted and recreated
The permanently closed period can simply be reopened and edited
The correction must be posted to a different, open period — permanently closed cannot be undone
Nothing — permanently closed periods accept new journals automatically
questions.explain: Permanently Closed is irreversible; corrections go into a currently open period instead.

questions.q: Why do duplicate party records tend to happen in HZ_PARTIES?
options: HZ_PARTIES automatically merges identical companies, so duplicates are impossible
Because parties are entered by people, the same real-world company can be entered more than once with slightly different names or addresses
Because HZ_PARTIES only stores one row per customer by design
Because duplicate parties are generated automatically by Subledger Accounting
questions.explain: Manual, inconsistent data entry (e.g. "Acme Corp" vs. "Acme Corporation") is the classic source of duplicate party records in Trading Community Architecture.

questions.q: How can OTBI subject areas help validate a hand-built data map?
options: They can't — OTBI is unrelated to the underlying tables
Subject areas are built on views over the same base tables, so how they group fields can hint at real underlying relationships
OTBI subject areas replace the need for any table documentation
OTBI only works with Receivables data
questions.explain: Because OTBI subject areas sit on views over the same base tables, their field groupings can serve as a sanity check on relationships traced by hand.
